 Smt.Rachna Dogra & Anr. Versus Spicejet Limited & Anr.
 F.A. No.68/2020

Ms.Sunita Sharma, Presiding Member :

O R D E R :
-
1. Present appeal has been filed against the order

dated 02.11.2019 passed by Learned District Consumer

Forum/Commission, Shimla, H.P. in consumer complaint

No.52/2018, titled Smt.Rachna Dogra & Anr. Versus Spice jet

Limited & Anr.
Brief facts of consumer complaint:
2. The case of the complainant in brief is that

complainants have booked tickets of Spice jet SD-971

through OP No.2 from Delhi to Trivandrum to attend the

National Shooting Championship which was going to be held

from 11.12.2017 to 16.12.2017 and they paid amount of

Rs.30,885/- and the flight of the complainants was on

10.12.2017 from Indira Gandhi Airport Delhi to Trivandrum

at 7:45 AM and the complainants were required to reach the

airport before half an hour as per the instructions. It is

further pleaded that the complainants reached at the airport

in the morning at 5 o'clock and on inquiry they were

surprised when they came to know that their flight has been

cancelled and the complainants thereafter asked for any

alternative arrangement or alternative flight but the Executive

of the OP No.1 refused for any such flight or arrangement and

the complainants thereafter inquired as to why they have not
2
Smt.Rachna Dogra & Anr. Versus Spicejet Limited & Anr.
F.A. No.68/2020
been sent any message in advance so that they could have

made alternative arrangement but no satisfactory reply was

given by the Executive of the OP No. 1. It is further pleaded

that the complainants also asked the OP No. 1 to refund the

cost of the ticket so that they could make other arrangements

to reach Trivandrum well in time but the Executive refused to

do so and misbehaved with the complainants and thereafter

the complainants were forced to book five tickets amounting

to Rs.74,695/- for the flight which was available at 9:15 PM

as all other flights were already booked and was the last flight

of the day to reach the destination in time and failure of the

OP No.1 to intimate the complainants well in time regarding

the cancellation of their flight amounts to deficiency in service

due to which the complainants were compelled to pay

Rs.44,000/- extra and they have also suffered harassment as

well as mental agony.
3. The complaint so filed has been opposed by the OP

No.1 by filing reply taking preliminary objections therein

regarding maintainability. On merits, it is pleaded that the

flight dated 10.12.2017 from Delhi to Trivandrum has been

cancelled due to change in schedule regarding which

intimation was given to the passengers including the

complainants by way of SMS on the provided mobile

No.09459584377 as well as by way of e-mail on the e-mail
3
Smt.Rachna Dogra & Anr. Versus Spicejet Limited & Anr.
F.A. No.68/2020
address provided. It is further pleaded that the said tickets

were booked by the complainants through OP No.2 and a sum

of Rs.29,635/- i.e. the total amount of the tickets has been

refunded to the OP No. 2 by OP No. 1 on 12.12.2017 itself

and since intimation regarding cancellation of flight has been

given to all the passengers including the complainants in

advance, no cause of action has arisen in favour of the

complainants to file the present complaint and as such OP

No. 1 is not liable for non-operation of the flight in question. It

is denied that there is any deficiency in service on the part of

the OP No.1
4. OP No.2 filed separate reply taking preliminary

objections therein regarding maintainability and cause of

action. On merits, it is not denied that the complainant has

booked a flight from Delhi to Trivandrum via Kochi which

flight was to be operated by the OP No. 1 on 10.12.2017. It is

also not denied that the flight, which was to be operated by

the OP No.1 has been cancelled on that date, but pleaded that

the OP No. 2 is not liable for any delay or cancellation of the

flight as the flight is being operated by OP No.1. It is further

pleaded that OP No.2 was not under any obligation to provide

any alternative arrangement to the complainants and the

grievance of the complainants is limited to the cancellation of

the confirmed flight by OP No.1 and not on account of any
4
Smt.Rachna Dogra & Anr. Versus Spicejet Limited & Anr.
F.A. No.68/2020
mistake on the part of OP No. 2. It is also pleaded that the

complainants informed the OP No.2 about the cancellation of

the tickets by the OP No.1 post travel date seeking refund on

cancelled tickets on which the OP No.2 contacted OP No.1

and OP No.1 never gave a concrete reason for cancellation of

the flight and since flight of the complainant was cancelled by

the OP No. 1, thus the complainants were eligible for refund

which was transferred by the OP No. 1 to the OP No. 2 and

accordingly the entire amount of Rs.30,589/- was refunded to

the complainants on 13.12.2017 by the OP No. 2 and thus

there is no deficiency in service on the part of OP No. 2.
5. No rejoinder was filed on behalf of complainants.
6. The parties led oral as well as documentary

evidence in support of their respective claims before learned

District Commission.
7. The learned District Commission below after

hearing the parties and going through the record partly

allowed the complaint and the OP No.1 was directed to refund

Rs.44,000/- to the complainants, which the complainants

were forced to spend extra on account of purchasing of tickets

of another flight along with interest @ 9% per annum from the

date of filing of complaint till its payment. The OP No.1 was

further directed to pay Rs.25,000/- as compensation for
5
Smt.Rachna Dogra & Anr. Versus Spicejet Limited & Anr.
F.A. No.68/2020
mental agony and harassment and further sum of Rs.5,000/-

as costs of litigation.
8. Feeling aggrieved by the order passed by learned

District Forum below, the complainants filed the instant

appeal for enhancement of the compensation amount for

mental agony and harassment from Rs.25,000/- to

Rs.50,000/- and also for enhancement of litigation costs from

Rs.5,000/- to Rs.15,000/-.
9. We have heard learned Advocates appearing on

behalf of appellants and the respondent No.2. None appeared

on behalf of respondent No.1 before State Commission. We

have also perused the entire record carefully.
10. Following points arise for determination in present

appeal.
1. Whether appeal filed by appellants is liable to be
 accepted as mentioned in memorandum of
 grounds of appeal?
2. Final order.
Findings upon point No.1 with reasons:
11. Learned counsel for the appellants argued that as

the District Commission below has held that there was

deficiency in service on the part of the respondent No.1, who

was to operate the flight, in its failure to inform the

complainants regarding cancellation of flight well in advance,

the compensation awarded by District Commission to the

tune of Rs.25,000/- is on very lower side as also the litigation
6
Smt.Rachna Dogra & Anr. Versus Spicejet Limited & Anr.
F.A. No.68/2020
costs of Rs.5,000/- and same requires to be enhanced. He

prayed that appeal be allowed and the compensation amount

be enhanced from Rs.25,000/- to Rs.50,000/- and litigation

costs from Rs.5,000/- to Rs.15,000/-.
12. None appeared on behalf of respondent No.1 to

address arguments before State Commission.
13. Learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has

defended the order of the learned District Commission and

also argued that there was no deficiency in service or unfair

trade practice on behalf of respondent No.2.
14. It has proved on record that despite appellants

having confirmed/OK tickets from the respondent No.1, flight

has been cancelled by the respondent No.1 without giving any

plausible reason as well as prior intimation well in advance.

It has also proved on record that the respondent No.1 did not

provide alternate and immediate flight to the appellants to

reach their destination and the appellants were forced to

spend extra amount on account of purchasing of tickets of

another flight.
15. In the case in hand, the complainants both are

women had O.K. tickets in their possession and they could

not imagine that on reaching the airport, they will be

confronted with the situation that their flight had been

cancelled leaving them in a lurch, because they did not belong

to Delhi and had to attend the tournament at Trivandrum.
7
Smt.Rachna Dogra & Anr. Versus Spicejet Limited & Anr.
F.A. No.68/2020
Intimation regarding cancellation of their flight on reaching at

Indira Gandhi Airport Delhi must have come as life time

unpleasant surprise to them. It is not difficult to visualize the

kind of mental trauma they would have suffered during those

hours. The appellant No.2 who was brilliant shooter and was

going to attend National Championship at Trivandrum must

have been thinking about losing her opportunity to participate

in the National level championship and the appellant No. 1

who is mother of appellant No. 2 must have also under shock

who had been preparing her for the last so many years to

become a champion. Though their mental stress cannot be

compensated, but still they deserve compensation from the

respondent No1, which they have claimed.
16. It has also proved on record that the respondent

No.1 did not bother to make alternate arrangement or

alternate flight for the appellants despite the fact that they

were having confirmed OK tickets with them. It was the plea

of the respondent No.1 before learned Commission that

intimation was given to the complainants regarding

cancellation of the flight by way of SMS on the mobile number

provided by the complainants. But, the complainants have

specifically averred that they have never received any SMS

from the respondent No.1 regarding cancellation of flight. But

from the perusal of Annexure R-2 i.e. the SMS alleged to have

been sent to the complainants regarding cancellation of flight,
8
Smt.Rachna Dogra & Anr. Versus Spicejet Limited & Anr.
F.A. No.68/2020
it is clear that the SMS so sent was never forwarded/ received

by the complainants as SMS alert so sent on the mobile

number of the complainants is shows to have failed, which in

itself belies the plea of the respondent No.1 that complainants

were duly informed regarding the cancellation of flight. This

also shows that respondent No.1 has shown casual approach

towards its customers and they were deficient in providing

services to its customers. The appellants deserve a better

treatment from National Carrier like respondent No1.
17. Thus, keeping in view of the above facts and

circumstances of the case, it is proved on regard that

respondent No.1 has not only committed grave unfair trade

practice by cancelling the flight especially when

OK/confirmed tickets were supplied to the complainants, but

act and conduct also amounts to adoption of malpractice and

deficiency in service. As such, we are of the considered view

that compensation amount and also the litigation costs

awarded by learned District Commission are required to be

enhanced. Point No.1 is decided accordingly.

Point No.2: Final Order
18. In view of findings upon point No.1 above, appeal

filed by complainants/appellants is allowed and order of

learned District Commission is modified to the extent that

respondent No.1 shall pay sum of Rs.25,000/- as
9
Smt.Rachna Dogra & Anr. Versus Spicejet Limited & Anr.
F.A. No.68/2020
compensation to complainants in addition to the

compensation awarded by District Commission. It is further

ordered that respondent No.1 shall pay litigation costs to the

tune of Rs.10,000/- to complainants in addition to the costs

awarded by District Commission. As regards the order of

learned District Commission regarding refund of Rs.44,000/-

to the complainants, which the complainants were forced to

spend extra on account of purchasing of tickets of another

flight along with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of

filing of complaint till its payment, the same is affirmed.
19. Certified copy of order be transmitted to parties

forthwith free of costs strictly as per rules. Certified copy of

order be sent to learned District Commission below forthwith

for information and file of State Commission be consigned to

record room after due completion forthwith. F.A.No.68/2020

is disposed of. Pending application(s) if any also disposed of.

 Presiding Member
